subject.title: Bound plugin bundle command file reads with size cap

question: Should installed Claude bundle command Markdown have a universal 1 MiB hard limit that disables larger existing commands, and if so what diagnostic/upgrade contract should users receive?
rationale: The shared reader is appropriate for bounding hostile input, but the chosen limit changes a previously accepted plugin-content contract and no current source or test establishes that legitimate command templates fit within it.

options.title: Adopt the 1 MiB contract with diagnostics
options.body: Keep the cap, add a clear warning naming the skipped file and cap, cover the boundary behavior, and treat larger command templates as unsupported.

options.title: Choose a different bounded contract
options.body: Select a limit or loading design that bounds memory while preserving the expected size range for installed command templates.

recommendation.title: Adopt the 1 MiB contract with diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep the cap, add a clear warning naming the skipped file and cap, cover the boundary behavior, and treat larger command templates as unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the immediately related bounded-reader implementation and can supply the relevant context, though feature ownership remains uncertain.
